A consumer may compare a price with a filed LEVEL; it never re-derives a lens STATE or EVENT. Every filed Stage V table is asserted against the sha in Stage V's progress record before use." findings.fix: Replace L-R.14's refusal list: "An event is REFUSED and counted, before the reward test, iff (1) stop_none; (2) d·(T1 − e) ≤ 0 — the POC is not ahead of the entry (poc_not_ahead; the contract's 'toward the POC', :70); (3) d·(T2 − e) ≤ 0 (t2_not_ahead). There is no fee band: the contract's only skip is 'rr-min' (:73). A T1 within 10 bps of the entry is traded as written and counted (t1_within_fee_band, with tenbps_r printed). d·(T2 − T1) ≤ 0 is not a refusal: T1 is VOID and T2 takes the whole position (t1_void, counted) — L-S.11's law, one law for both range rows." X's law (the 10 bps band and the inverted-targets refusal) is printed as the Tier-E arm tierE__x_geometry, re-walked with its own one-position sequence, with the rows that differ listed; F-SFP-MIRROR keeps X's law on X's filed rows. Amend the spec's Refused clause, L-R.19 (no T1 fill on a void T1), L-R.24, and L-R.32 (the fee-band row moves to the twin). L-S INTERFACE to L-R: the three stated differences drop to two.

findings.finding: L-S.27 item 2 invents a second closing condition for P-SCALP-3: "The licence at the pinned maker rate … The item re-derives the row's edge leg at that rate … edge_net_at_pin = round(edge_median_term_h20, 8) − round(edge_toll_atr × (2·maker_bps_side / toll_bps), 8); required > 0", else "CLOSED_BY_PRECONDITION … and NOTHING else: no candidate, no order, no book". It is in the registration spec's preconditions. The contract's only licence is the mirror word (:39-41). O-19 rules the handling of a different maker rate: "that is printed beside the '1h maker PASS' word". O-17: "THE MIRROR READS, NEVER RECOMPUTES". The item is a partial recompute ("share_ratio_lt_1 cannot be re-derived from printed columns and is carried as read"), reads a block L-V.17 does not file ("until it does, builder and scorer compute it"), has no filed precedent, and prints no rival, since a closed row prints nothing. The section concedes the divergence without an OBJECTION block ("the ruling does not forbid it") and lists the ruling's own reading as "the alternative only the operator can order". L-X.10 states "On the records as filed no item fails", which this item contradicts ("undetermined until Stage D's fee capture").
findings.consequence: An executor-made rule can erase, with no number and no test spent, the one row that "exists by the 'maker' ruling" (:82), on a hybrid licence X never filed. A row that would read NOT SUPPORTED becomes a free closure.
findings.fix: Delete item 2 from L-S.27 and from the spec's preconditions; one item remains (licence["1h|maker"].by_era["holdout"].would_read == "PASS"). Add to L-S.27: "Printed beside the licence word in the verdict text and in §0.3, deciding nothing (O-19): Stage D's pinned maker_bps_side, X's assumed round trip (toll_bps), maker_pin.differs_from_x_assumption, and — iff they differ — edge_net_at_pin by the linear toll law, labelled 'a re-derivation of one leg from printed columns; not a licence'." Strike the two additions asked of L-V (the at_maker_pin block) and F-SCALP (p)'s fee-file plant. OPEN TO OPERATOR 2 becomes: "A published maker rate at which X's edge leg is not above zero. DEFAULT if silent: the row is built and scored, with the re-derived figure printed beside the word (O-19). Closing the row on it is the operator's order."

findings.finding: Stage R re-runs the Stage V door from its own suite and carries a second copy of the V2 machine in a builder. L-R.7 (c): "the 4h state from the DOOR re-run on the 4h tape cut at τ … equals the filed state the gate read". L-R.25 F-SFP-ASOF: "the DOOR re-run on the 4h tape cut at the event's known_close_ms reproduces the event row". L-R.29: "The machine on a box — a mirror of static_box_machine with V2's three constants in place of the pivot's (DEV_RETURN_BARS → K, BREAK_CONFIRM_N → N, BREAK_MARGIN → M)", living in scripts/tierc12_stage_r_tables.py and held by F-NULL-MIRROR (b) against "value_area.va_machine … (a fixture may import the module; no builder does)". O-29: analytics.value_area "is imported only by the Stage V door scripts and their fixtures"; a consumer "never re-derives a lens STATE or EVENT". L-R.17's own RIVALS rejects "a second state machine outside the module".
findings.consequence: The Stage R suite imports the door and the module (RED under O-29's closure fixture, or an unruled exemption), and the acceptance and swing-failure law exists twice. The null's events can drift from V2 with only a seeded-sample fixture between them.
findings.fix: (1) Cut-tape legs move to Stage V's suite. Stage R files its key lists (the base campaigns' entry closes; the seeded swing-failure events); a dotted child TC12-V.asof-r runs scripts/tierc12_va_fixtures.py on those keys, re-runs the door on tapes cut at each instant and files va/ASOF_REFEREE_R.parquet, sha-pinned in that record. L-R.7 (c) and F-SFP-ASOF compare filed rows with that table and import nothing of Stage V. (2) The gaps+order null is run by the door. Add to L-V.23: "the gaps+order@va_regime generator: the mirrored schedule (tierc10_null.schedule, read as text) over va_regimes, then value_area.va_machine on arrays held constant at each box's edges; filed as va/va_null_box_events.parquet and va/NULL_BOXES_VA.parquet for 4h and 1d × the five home assets." L-R.29 keeps the conditioning and the per-draw statistics, computed from those filed rows. F-NULL-MIRROR (a) and (c) move to Stage V's suite; leg (b) is deleted (no mirrored machine remains).

findings.finding: L-X.24: "Cross-arm law on P-SCALP-3: n(ladder__touch) ≥ n(scored) ≥ n(ladder__deep), else HALT LADDER-ORDER." L-S.16 builds the three books with separate order sequences and shows the totals are not ordered by construction: "Book totals are printed and are NOT a theorem … a touch-only fill can block triggers the record would have traded … That flag is a disclosure, never a HALT". O-32 rules DEEP "so the contract's own ordering fixture can hold per order". The conflict is flagged in L-S's INTERFACE and left to "the reviser".
findings.consequence: The scorer can HALT P-SCALP-3 (no number, no word, CLOSE blocked) on a book-total inversion that is not a defect; or a builder guesses which section governs.
findings.fix: L-X.24, replace the cross-arm law: "Cross-arm law on P-SCALP-3 (per order, O-32): each ladder and scored sidecar carries n_orders, n_filled_touch, n_filled_tick, n_filled_deep evaluated on that ledger's own orders; HALT LADDER-ORDER unless n_filled_touch ≥ n_filled_tick ≥ n_filled_deep on every ledger. The three arm totals n(ladder__touch), n(scored), n(ladder__deep) are printed in the fill-sensitivity row, and BOOK-N-NOT-MONOTONE is a disclosure flag, never a HALT." F-REGBOOK plant: swapped per-order counts → LADDER-ORDER.

findings.finding: L-V.19: "Stage V files no per-book table … Each book stage calls the reader's stamp(instants_of(frame, kind)) on its own frame and files VA_STAMPS_<book>.parquet in its own stage directory … recorded in its own progress record". L-C.11 files it under "the sub-stage TC12-C.stamps" in T12/books/; L-R.31 in stage_r/; L-S.30 in stage_s/. L-0's INTERFACE: "L-V's TC12-V5 … is, under L-0.10, a dotted child of that book's own stage". O-29 lists "the instant stamps" among the door's FILED tables, "each sha-pinned in Stage V's progress record and asserted before use"; O-31 names the child: "TC12-V.stamps".
findings.consequence: Four sections pin the stamp tables in four different progress records, none of them Stage V's. A consumer (L-L.16's side table, L-R.4's entry-row assertion) has no single record to assert against, and the stage id contradicts O-31.
findings.fix: L-V.19, "Who files what": "The instant stamps are Stage V tables (O-29), filed under the dotted child TC12-V.stamps (O-31). After a book stage files its campaign frame, the reader is run on that frame and files va/stamps/VA_STAMPS_<book>.parquet; progress/TC12-V.stamps.json records every such table {bytes, sha256} and names in depends_on the book stage whose frame it read. A consumer asserts the sha against that record before use. No book builder stamps its own book." L-0.10: "a dotted child may depend on stages later than its parent; its record's depends_on is what L-0.4's quarantine rule follows"; replace the INTERFACE sentence on TC12-V5. Conform L-C.11 (TC12-C.stamps → TC12-V.stamps; T12/books/VA_STAMPS_* → T12/va/stamps/), L-G.18, L-R.31, L-S.30, L-L.16 and L-L.25 paths.

findings.finding: L-D.25 files the vendored referee "with TC12-REG under the progress record TC12-REG.vendor … before any hunk is applied"; L-D.30 orders "TC12-REG.vendor (the referee committed; its three-sha equality) → TC12-D → TC12-ENV"; L-0.10 gives the example "a frozen referee text: TC12-REG.vendor" and L-0's INTERFACE repeats it. O-31: sub-stages are "(TC12-D.mirror, TC12-ENV.vendor, TC12-V.stamps) … The env shim is vendored and proven inside TC12-ENV, after TC12-D."
findings.consequence: The referee would be committed at the registration stage under an id the ruling does not recognise, and F-RESUME / F-COMMIT ("a subject does not name an ORDER stage", stage records in ORDER) would be built to the wrong order.
findings.fix: Replace TC12-REG.vendor by TC12-ENV.vendor everywhere. L-D.25: "filed under the progress record TC12-ENV.vendor, the first act of TC12-ENV, after TC12-D is COMPLETE-VERIFIED and before any hunk is applied". L-D.30 order: "TC12-D (L-D.5 steps 1-7) → TC12-ENV.vendor (the referee committed; its three-sha equality) → TC12-ENV". L-0.10: "a frozen referee text: TC12-ENV.vendor". L-0 INTERFACE and L-D INTERFACE likewise; the TC12-REG row of L-0.10's stage table gains nothing from L-D.

findings.finding: The contract's V4 measures travel "edge-to-edge while INSIDE" (:42), and V2 defines INSIDE as a state (:34). L-V.18 widens it: "'While INSIDE' = within a value regime. Bars of a probe that fails or lapses are inside the leg … the count of legs containing a PROBING bar is printed." The literal reading is dismissed in RIVALS ("(f) state INSIDE on every bar of the leg — voids every leg that follows a failed probe") and its T is never printed; only a count of the affected legs is. T is the time stop of record of P-SFP-VA-1 and P-SCALP-3.
findings.consequence: The time stop of two registered rows rests on a population wider than the contract's words, and the reader cannot see what the widening is worth in bars: a degree of freedom with its rival unprinted.
findings.fix: Add to L-V.18's "Printed beside, Tier-E, no pin": "and the contract's phrase read strictly: the same statistic over the tuning legs with n_probe_bars == 0 (every bar of the leg INSIDE after its close) — T_strict_inside, n_legs_strict, the hinges, per lens, in TRAVERSE.json under twins.strict_inside and in STAGE_V.md beside T_of_record". State in the reading: "T of record uses the regime reading; the strict reading is a printed twin and enters no book." F-TRAV (b) re-derives both from traverse_legs.parquet.

findings.finding: The contract's kill has two clauses that both hold when TICK fails, DEEP fails and TOUCH clears: "CLOSED FOR GOOD if it fails under DEEP too; CLOSED if it clears only under TOUCH" (:104-105). L-X.9 gives that case the milder word ("| false | any | false | true | NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED | (clears only under TOUCH) |") on the ground that "the clause that names that event exactly … governs it, and 'FOR GOOD' is left for the book that fails under every fill model". The literal first clause would read CLOSED FOR GOOD regardless of TOUCH. The choice is in neither section's OPEN TO OPERATOR and not among O-32's standing defaults, and L-S.28 attaches lasting consequences to the difference ("closed in this and every later tier; no fill model reopens it").
findings.consequence: A registered row's verdict word, and what the ledger append forbids afterwards, turns on an executor choice between two readings of the operator's sentence, taken toward the milder closure and never shown to the operator.
findings.fix: Keep the table, list the choice, and print both clause truths. L-X OPEN TO OPERATOR, new item: "CLOSED versus CLOSED FOR GOOD when TICK and DEEP fail and TOUCH clears. Both contract clauses hold there. Default if silent: NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED (clears only under TOUCH), so that each clause has a live event; the literal-order rival (CLOSED FOR GOOD whenever TICK and DEEP fail) is the operator's to name." L-X.9 and L-S.28: the verdict text and SCORES.json rows[].fill_ladder carry two booleans, fails_under_deep_too and clears_only_under_touch, printed in the fill-sensitivity row. Mirror the item in L-S OPEN TO OPERATOR.

findings.finding: L-0.26's fixture forbids what L-X must write and run. F-NOT leg ACTS "FAILS IF any TC12 source, fixtures included, holds an argv or shell string whose git subcommand is push or merge, an import publish_exchange …, a call named publish"; and the reading says of close_acts.sh "its only executions are bash -n and its step 0 against scratch repositories". L-X.33's generator emits "Step 1 · git push origin v12-v1-census" and "Step 8 · publish()", and its F-CLOSE-SCRIPT runs "steps 1-7 … in a sandbox clone against a local bare origin". L-X lists the three differences "for the reviser to rule" (also L-0.16's registered marker against L-X.28 §4); none is ruled. O-12 forbids the executor running the acts and says nothing of a scratch copy.
findings.consequence: As drafted the close generator turns F-NOT RED by construction, and whether the order of the acts is proven by a sandbox run or only by a static law is left to whoever builds TC12-CLOSE.
findings.fix: L-0.26 READING, replace the sentence: "its only executions are bash -n and runs of a SCRATCH COPY with every path and cwd asserted outside both trees: step 0 (--check) against scratch repositories, and steps 1-7 against a sandbox clone with a local bare origin, cut before publish() (L-X.33's F-CLOSE-SCRIPT; TC11's F-CLOSE-ORDER form). The generated file in the main tree is never executed." F-NOT leg ACTS, add: "EXEMPT by a typed list of one: the string constants of scripts/tierc12_close_acts_template.py, which holds the text of close_acts.sh and nothing else (no call, no subprocess, no import beyond __future__; imported only by the close generator) and is held by F-CLOSE-SCRIPT's static law." Planted mutations: a git push string in any other TC12 source → RED; a call added to the template module → UNEARNED RED. L-0.16: the registered marker is allowed in "score documents, §0, and §4's verbatim re-quote of P-SCALP-3's verdict text (L-X.28)". Delete the three-differences paragraph from L-X's INTERFACE.

findings.finding: L-S.30 asserts "Every order and trade table is a per-trade or per-asset row file for L-L's ferry (contract :111)", and its INTERFACE classes "S_orders_*, S_refusals_*, S_miss, the eight arms and VA_STAMPS_scalp (per-trade row files, CSV, 2 MB cap …)". L-L.24 freezes X's vocabulary: the identity instant is "the first present of entry_ms, entry_open_ms, entry_close_ms, harden_ms, event_ms, known_at_ms" (x_rec/scripts/tc11x_ferry.py:195), and "A TC12 table that wants to be ferried is built to the vocabulary". L-S's tables are keyed on trigger_close_ms (S_orders and S_refusals: "[book, symbol, trigger_close_ms]"; S_miss: "[symbol, trigger_close_ms, target]"), which is not one of the six, and target is not one of the 26 axis words. L-L.25 already types "every VA_STAMPS_<book>.parquet" POINTED.
findings.consequence: Under L-L.24's rule the scalper's order, refusal and MISS tables class as POINTED ("rows per identity > 1"), so the contract's "MISS COLUMN first-class" rows never enter the ferry although L-S says they do; or the assembler re-types them by hand, which L-L.25 forbids ("no drafter chooses it").
findings.fix: L-S.30 table: S_orders_<book> and S_refusals_<book> key "[book, symbol, known_at_ms]" with known_at_ms = the trigger close (trigger_close_ms kept as an alias column); neither table carries a column named entry_ms, entry_open_ms or entry_close_ms (the fill is fill_close_ms). S_miss key "[symbol, known_at_ms, variant]", variant ∈ {T1, T2, split}. Replace the sentence at the end of L-S.30 by: "Ferry classes are derived by L-L.24's rule from these declared columns: the arms, S_orders_*, S_refusals_*, S_miss and open_at_w_continued are PER-TRADE (FERRIED); VA_STAMPS_scalp and the grids are POINTED (L-L.25)." Correct the INTERFACE line the same way; L-L.25 gains the rows at assembly.

findings.finding: L-V.8 rule 2 states a universal that L-V.9 breaks: "Bar t's close, high and low are JUDGED against VA(t−1) … Every state, event, %-of-value, distance and touch in this section uses that frame", while L-V.9 judges every close of a pending probe "against E, not against the re-rolled VA" and consults VA(t−1) "not at all" while a probe is pending. O-16 (a) is written with the same universal ("every close at bar t is judged against VA(t−1)"), and L-V's OBJECTIONS says "None on the facts". L-V.13 (i) adds a state that departs from the contract's letter ("INSIDE: close within [VAL, VAH]", :34): after a resolution "the state is INSIDE by the frozen edge even when the close lies outside the rolling VA(t−1)". Neither departure is in the text of the dated amendment AM-V2.
findings.consequence: A builder reading L-V.8 or O-16 (a) literally implements X's moving_edge twin and fails F-STATE-X; and the scalper's PERMISSION can read INSIDE on an hour whose close is outside the rolling value with no count of how often.
findings.fix: L-V.8 rule 2: "An IDLE bar's close, and every bar's high and low, are judged against VA(t−1). A close while a probe is pending is judged against that probe's FROZEN edge, the edge of VA(t0−1) (L-V.9) — X's convention, which O-16 (a) names. Never the self-inclusive VA(t)." Add to L-V's OBJECTIONS an annotation of O-16 (a) in those words. Add to AM-V2: "Declared against the contract's letter: (i) pending closes are judged against the frozen edge; (ii) on a bar that resolves a probe the state is INSIDE by the frozen edge even where the close lies outside the rolling VA(t−1), counted per cell and filed per bar as inside_frozen_only." L-V.24's va_bars columns gain inside_frozen_only; L-S.4 prints the count of orders whose row k1 carries it.

findings.finding: Residue of rulings since accepted. L-D's two OBJECTION blocks still argue O-8 and O-20 as open, and the first keeps a live alternative: "If the orchestrator means the parenthesis literally, the change is one line (FIFTEEN leaves lenses_of)". O-26 and O-27 settled both. L-D.27's exchange-write row names "the three earlier contracts" where O-25 counts two in main. L-S.15 cites "L-D's OBJECTION O-20" where the ruling is now O-27. Every section header declares conformity to "O-1..O-24" (L-D: "O-1..O-9, O-14, O-19, O-20").
findings.consequence: A frozen LEANS that carries a superseded alternative and claims conformity only to O-1..O-24 lets a builder take the struck branch (dropping the five 15m tapes) or treat section H as outside the readings.
findings.fix: L-D OBJECTIONS: replace both blocks by one line each, "accepted as O-26" and "accepted as O-27", deleting the "Drafted under the ruling as written" alternatives. L-D.4 cites O-26 for the 124-path scope; L-D.22 cites O-27 for the UNVERIFIED "never looser". L-D.27: "the two earlier TC contracts (TC10 RESUME, TC11)". L-S.15: "O-27". Every section header: "conforms to ORCHESTRATOR_RULINGS O-1..O-32".

findings.finding: The contract stamps "every funnel instant of every book (base v6, 9/12, the gated books, every arm below)" (:44). L-R.31 covers only two cases: "P-DIR-1's kept book is a key subset of v6's instants" and "Each RIDDEN range book declares its instants frame". Two ridden arms fall in neither. tierE__reride (L-R.5) can hold campaigns "n_admitted_not_in_v6", which have no v6 instants. The TP-1d venue book (L-R.30) re-rides every base campaign with a new exit (exit_reason = "tp") whose instant is not in v6's stamp table.
findings.consequence: Those arms' new instants carry no VA vector, or a builder asserts the subset law on books that are not subsets and HALTs.
findings.fix: Add to L-R.31's stamps bullet: "tierE__reride and the TP-1d venue book are ridden books whose campaigns or exits are not all v6's. Each declares its instants frame (kind {lens 4h, start: arm}; v6's events plus ev_tp_ms — intrabar, the OPEN of its bar, with a post-event twin) and is stamped under TC12-V.stamps. A campaign identical to its v6 twin on every instant is asserted to be in v6's key set and is not re-stamped."

findings.finding: L-S.10 shows that a contract clause is dead and does not list it for the operator: "on a CROSS trigger the structural stop is L ∓ 0.5·ATR, the rail is L ∓ 1.0·ATR, the rail always binds, and R ≡ 1.0·ATR_1h on every cross-triggered order — the contract's '0.5 ATR_1h beyond the edge' never sets a stop." The contract writes both numbers in one sentence (:97-98). The reading is faithful, but an operator who meant a 0.5 ATR stop on cross triggers finds out only from a count in the stage document.
findings.consequence: A clause of the registered row's text has no effect on any trade and the operator is not asked whether that was meant. A veto after the look would carry the NOT CONFIRMATORY mark of L-0.23.
findings.fix: Add to L-S OPEN TO OPERATOR: "The stop's else-clause never binds. With the stop measured from the limit at the edge, '0.5 ATR_1h beyond the edge' (:97) is always inside the 1.0 ATR_1h rail (:98), so every cross-triggered order has R = 1.0·ATR_1h. DEFAULT if silent: the contract as written (the rail governs); the count of cross orders and rail_binding is printed. A cross stop at 0.5 ATR_1h with no rail is the operator's order."

findings.finding: L-R.27 reads: "L = 1d. Its lens above is 1w ... Drafted under the ruling as written: every 1d event is in cell `NA` (\"no conditioning lens: 1w is captured-only [O-11]\") and the other seven 1d cells are rows with `n = 0`". O-28 (filed after the draft) rules the opposite: the 1w value area "may be read in exactly two places, both Tier-E: the V5 stamp columns, and the lens-above conditioning axis of the 1d two-trades table (the contract's 'conditioned on the lens above' at :76-79 has no other object at 1d)". The draft therefore contradicts O-28 and, because it never reads 1w, states no as-of rule (instant, row, label) for the one 1w read the ruling permits.
findings.consequence: The 1d rows of the contract's two-trades table (:76-79) are printed unconditioned, contrary to O-28. If a builder adds the 1w read ad hoc there is no stated instant or row: the week still forming at a 1d close could be read, and the borrowed lookback would go unlabelled.
findings.fix: Replace the 'L = 1d' bullet of L-R.27 with: "L = 1d. U = 1w (O-28). U's block is row k = asof_index(close_ms_1w, τ) of `va_bars_1w` at the event's known-at close τ: the last COMPLETE Monday-anchored derived week whose close ≤ τ (a week still forming is never read; on a Monday 00:00Z close the week closing at τ IS read, O-14). The eight-cell partition applies unchanged, the coincidence unit being F·ATR_1d[k_event]; L-R.28's base rate (ii) reads 1d's own nest flag against 1w at close_k. Every 1d row of TWO_TRADES_VA / TWO_TRADES_BASE / TWO_TRADES_NULL carries `u_lookback_label = 'BORROWED: 1w built on the 1d pin's bar count (L-V.5)'`. No other L-R module reads a `1w_` column." Add to F-TWO (a) the plant 'the 1w bar still forming at τ read' -> RED. Delete OPEN TO OPERATOR 1 and the OBJECTION block (accepted as O-28).

findings.finding: L-0.25 (iii): "The 1w member of the V5 vector (:45) is a CAPTURED-ONLY stamp: printed on funnel instants under the collar, read by no gate, no permission, no direction guard, no conditioning axis", enforced by F-NOT leg 1W ("a decision module's typed list of VA columns read holds a 1w column" -> RED). O-28 permits exactly one conditioning read (the lens-above axis of the 1d two-trades table).
findings.consequence: Once L-R.27 conforms to O-28, F-NOT leg 1W turns RED on a ruled-in read, or the read is dropped to keep the leg GREEN. Either way the build contradicts the ruling.
findings.fix: L-0.25 (iii) becomes: "The 1w member of the V5 vector is read by no gate, no permission, no direction guard, no licence, no time stop and no registered construction. It may be read in exactly two places, both Tier-E (O-28): the V5 stamp columns, and the lens-above conditioning axis of Stage R's 1d two-trades table (`scripts/tierc12_stage_r_tables.py`; columns `1w_state`, `1w_val`, `1w_vah`, `1w_pct`, `1w_bar_close_ms`), each row labelled BORROWED." F-NOT leg 1W becomes: "FAILS IF a table holding a trade, order or event-outcome column has a row whose own lens is 1w; a decision module other than `tierc12_stage_r_tables.py` declares a 1w column; that module declares a 1w column outside the five named; or a registered arm's spec names one." Add the plant: a 1w condition added to a copy of the P-SFP-VA-1 builder -> RED.

findings.finding: L-D.28: "`E.load_asof_at(stem, iv, close_ms)` ... HALT unless `close_ms` is a 4h close and `≤ PIN_MS`"; F-ENV-ASOF (L-D.31) fails if "a `close_ms` that is not a 4h close ... is accepted". Three as-of legs of L-V need cuts that are not 4h closes. (1) F-TRAV (d): "the leg table rebuilt on FRESH tapes cut at ERA_CUT". ERA_CUT 1719791999000 is 2024-06-30T23:59:59Z, on no bar grid; the last 4h close at or before it is 20:00Z, yet the 1h bars closing 21:00, 22:00 and 23:00Z are tuning bars and can complete tuning legs of the 1h traverse. (2) F-VA-ASOF (a): "`VA(t)` from a FRESH tape cut after bar t (`load_asof_at`)" on 1h cells, where three of four closes are off the 4h grid. (3) F-NEST-ASOF (a): "every lens tape of the asset is cut at τ (`load_asof_at` ...)" for instants on the 5m clock.

findings.finding: L-S.27 item 2 makes a second CLOSING precondition out of a number TC12 computes: "The item re-derives the row's edge leg at that rate by the census's own linear toll law … `edge_net_at_pin = round(edge_median_term_h20, 8) − round(edge_toll_atr × (2·maker_bps_side / toll_bps), 8)`; required `> 0`". findings.fix: L-X.27 add: "A refile never drops a verdict. findings.finding: L-X.24: "**Cross-arm law on P-SCALP-3:** `n(ladder__touch) ≥ n(scored) ≥ n(ladder__deep)`, else HALT `LADDER-ORDER`." findings.finding: L-X.7 names only the fully degenerate gate: "A gate that refuses nothing (`kept == base` by key): flagged `TWO-SAMPLE-PREMISE` … NOT SUPPORTED, test spent." The kept-versus-all ruler is structurally unable to clear well before that. `tierc5.cluster_boot_diff` (scripts/tierc5.py:1200-1224) indexes both arms with ONE asset pick; a pick holding no asset with a refused campaign yields identical kept and base rows, so the draw is exactly 0 and counts in `#draws ≤ 0` (`_ci_from`, :1227-1235; L-X.6 "an exact zero counts"). With a = the number of declared assets holding at least one refused campaign, P(draw ≡ 0) = ((N−a)/N)^N; at N = 5 that is 1024/3125 = 0.328 for a = 1 and 243/3125 = 0.0778 for a = 2 — above the 0.05 bar and above the 5% the 5th percentile tolerates [count arithmetic; no book read]. A gate whose refusals sit on two or fewer of the five assets cannot read SUPPORTED whatever the outcomes. L-R leaves exactly this open for P-DIR-1: "UNVERIFIED: the count of v6 campaigns the gate refuses, and whether every home asset keeps at least one campaign (L-X.7's panel clause decides the word if not)".
findings.consequence: P-DIR-1 (or P-BRD-1) can print a bare NOT SUPPORTED that reads as evidence against the gate when the ruler could not have said yes; the rule for the case would be written after the refused cohort is seen.
findings.fix: L-X.7, after the TWO-SAMPLE-PREMISE bullet, add: "**REFUSAL SPREAD (count-only, decided before any outcome is read).** `a` = the number of declared assets holding ≥ 1 refused campaign; `z = Fraction((N − a)**N, N**N)` = the exact probability that a draw holds no refusing asset and is identically 0. Filed on every two-sample row: `refused_n`, `refused_assets`, `p_draw_identically_zero`, `n_draws_exact_zero`. If `z ≥ bar_f` the row carries the qualifier `REFUSALS ON a/N ASSETS — the ruler cannot clear (P(draw ≡ 0) = z ≥ bar)`; the word is NOT SUPPORTED and the test is spent (the undefined-counts-against law); the cell is never cited as evidence against the gate. `a = 0` is TWO-SAMPLE-PREMISE." Add the qualifier to L-X.9's qualifier list and to the exhaustive-words sentence of the three gate specs; add an F-VERDICT case (a synthetic gate refusing on two of five assets must carry it).

findings.finding: L-X.9 defines "`C(X)` = clauses (a) ∧ (b) ∧ (c) on book X … \"fails the bar\" = `not C(X)`" and L-X.7 adds "Clause (c) applies to each fill-ladder book of P-SCALP-3". So a ladder book whose ruler is UNDEFINED (PANEL INCOMPLETE or EMPTY BOOK) counts as a book that failed, and the six-case table can print `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` or `— CLOSED FOR GOOD` on it. L-S.28 then binds every later tier: "scalper mode on the 1h value area at the maker toll is closed in this and every later tier; no fill model reopens it (it fails at the most generous one)". For the SUPPORTED direction "undefined never supports" is right; for a permanent closure it asserts a failure no ruler measured.
findings.consequence: A permanent closure word and its standing ledger line could rest on a book with no row on one asset rather than on an interval, and the statement "it fails at the most generous one" would be false of the record.
findings.fix: L-X.9, after the definition of C(X), add: "`U(X)` = book X is not PANEL COMPLETE (its ruler is undefined); `F(X)` = X is PANEL COMPLETE and fails (a) or (b). SUPPORTED needs C(TICK) as before. A closure word needs a MEASURED failure: `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` iff F(TICK) ∧ F(DEEP) ∧ C(TOUCH); `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED FOR GOOD` iff F(TICK) ∧ F(DEEP) ∧ F(TOUCH); with F(TICK) ∧ F(DEEP) ∧ U(TOUCH) the word is `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` with the qualifier `TOUCH PANEL INCOMPLETE — \"for good\" not ruled`; with U(TICK) or U(DEEP) the word is `NOT SUPPORTED` with the qualifier `<book> PANEL INCOMPLETE — closure not ruled`, and nothing is closed." Carry the same sentence into the spec's `verdict_rule` and extend F-VERDICT's LADDER leg from two states per book to three (C / F / U).

findings.finding: The statistic printed for the stage-shipped Tier-E arms is undeclared, and the sections disagree. No p, no bar, no sensitivity seed, no LOAO |" and the sentence "The declared beside set of a row = the common slugs + `arm__<slug>` for exactly the tierE arms named in its `disclosed_beside`; an arm without a leaf, or a leaf without an arm, is F-GRID RED. P-SCALP-3's `full_corridor` is `arm__full_corridor`." Replace the m_looks sentence by "`m_looks_this_table` = the number of intervals (lo, hi pairs) in `beside[]`, every LOAO panel counted; §1 prints the tier total over all collared tables beside the five tests." findings.finding: The five-cluster size warning is not bound to any row. findings.finding: L-L.17 leaves the forward score's row set to a later scorer: "when a later registration scores a forward book at `n ≥ n_min`, it MUST either exclude every row flagged `in_o9_scored_window` or print the score with and without them. The flagged rows count in `n` meanwhile; the choice between excluding and disclosing is that registration's, made before its look" (and the same for `entered_before_gate_text_filed`). findings.consequence: The contract's only confirmation of P-ADM-1 (:55-56) can later be scored on rows that predate its gate text, with the include/exclude choice made after every row's R is public, and can reach n ≥ 30 mostly on such rows.
findings.fix: L-L.17, replace the standing line by: "The row set of record for any later score is fixed HERE, in `BOOK_SPEC_COMBINED.json → n_law`, before a strip bar is on disk: rows with `in_o9_scored_window == false` and, for `gated-v6-combined`, `entered_before_gate_text_filed == false`. The all-rows figure is printed beside under the collar. No later registration chooses." L-L.14: the status line prints `n` (the contract's count, :110) and `n_record` (rows of the set above), and adds "of which <n_record> are rows of record for a forward score". L-L.10: the two flags become chained row fields (`row_fields_added` = five); both are pin-independent functions of `entry_close_ms` and two frozen instants. P-ADM-1's `disclosed_beside` clause: replace "opened on the chain before any strip bar was on disk" by "every row appended at TC12's pin entered before the gate text was filed (flagged on the row); none is a row of record for confirmation".

findings.finding: The two `selection_hazard` rows are labelled "direction-informed" without the one count that says whether the label is sufficient. P-BRD-1: D-1 records that the OUTCOME of a near-identical gate was seen at the contract's cut (17-asset breadth below 0.4: n 76 mean −0.154; at or above: n 121 mean +0.4365). How much of P-BRD-1's five-asset refused set is that seen cohort is computed (L-G.15's `G-BRD17`, "six cells, printed whole — the agreement of the twin with the row of record") but stays a Stage G Tier-E table; L-X.13 puts only D-1 under the cell. P-DIR-1: L-R.6 says "the direction of the refusal was chosen with R5 in view" and cites cell means (research_outputs/tierc11/stage_r/R5_CHOP.md:120-121: EXP_COUNTER n 12 mean −0.4939 on these same 200 campaigns), but no reading prints how many refused campaigns ARE those twelve. O-30: "A LABEL MUST BE TRUE".
findings.consequence: If either refused set is mostly a cohort whose mean was already printed, the row is in effect a re-score and "direction-informed" is true only by omission; a reader of §0 cannot tell.
findings.fix: L-X.13 add: "A `selection_hazard` row whose label cites a filed cohort outcome prints, directly under its cell, the KEY OVERLAP between its refused set and that cohort — counts only, no outcome. P-BRD-1 (under D-1): the six cells of `stage_g/g_brd17.parquet`. P-DIR-1: `n_refused`, and of those the number in TC11 R5's `EXP_COUNTER` and `EXP_ALIGNED` cells (pivot state at the entry instant: a mirror of `align_of`, scripts/tierc11_stage_r.py:1650-1661, on `research_outputs/tierc11/stage_r/NEST_v6.parquet`, calibrated 4h). F-S0-FIVE is RED when either line is absent." L-G.13 and L-R.6 name the count and its source; the `tierE__brd17` leaf carries the note "outcome of this split seen at R0 (D-1)".

findings.finding: P-ADM-1's label says what the test adds ("the new information is the interval of the difference from v6") but not the two facts that bound what its word can mean. (i) The point estimate of the row's own statistic is fixed by filed numbers before scoring: the kept book's mean (STAGE_G.md:197) minus the v6 mean (BASE_IDENT.json). (ii) The family bar here (q ÷ 2) is looser than the bar under which both halves were scored on these same 200 campaigns in TC11 (q ÷ 9): D-4 notes stale-alone's filed p "would clear a 0.05 bar", and TC11's P-AGE-1 arms are kept 141 of 200 with p_num/p_den 1/4001 on file.
findings.consequence: A SUPPORTED on this row could be read as stronger than TC11's verdicts although it is the same campaigns at a looser bar with a known point.
findings.fix: In `labels.pre_seen.text`, before "confirmation, if any, …", insert: "the point estimate of this row's statistic is fixed by filed numbers before scoring (the kept book's mean on file minus the v6 mean on file); the bar of this family (q ÷ 2) is looser than the bar under which both halves were scored on these campaigns in TC11 (q ÷ 9); a SUPPORTED here adds an interval to a seen effect and no evidence beyond TC11's;".

findings.finding: Two wording gaps in the ladder. (a) TOUCH and DEEP are ruled at the family bar with interval, `p_num/p_den` and a `C(X)` boolean printed inside §0, and are exempted from the collar (L-X.9: "a named exception to the Tier-E collar"; L-X.14 adds them to REGISTERED_TABLES_T, which L-0.16's own definition does not list). This is not a multiplicity toward SUPPORTED ("only the TICK book can"), but it is two uncorrected looks that choose among failure words, and the verdict text never says a TOUCH or DEEP interval excluding zero is not a result (contract :7). (b) For TICK and DEEP failing with TOUCH clearing, both contract clauses apply (:104-105); L-X.9 takes the softer word ("the clause that names that event exactly … governs") and lists the harsher only as RIVAL (i), not in OPEN TO OPERATOR, and O-32 does not list it among the standing defaults.
findings.consequence: A reader may cite the TOUCH book's interval as a finding; the operator is not shown a default that decides between a reopenable and a permanent closure.
findings.fix: L-X.9 "One test" bullet, add: "The fill-sensitivity row opens with the fixed sentence: 'TOUCH and DEEP are fill-model twins, not tests: they are ruled at the family bar without a test of their own and can only qualify a SUPPORTED cell or choose among the failure words; an interval that excludes zero on either is not a result.'" L-0.16: add "and the arms a registered row's verdict_rule reads (P-SCALP-3's `ladder__touch`, `ladder__deep`)" to the definition of a registered table. L-X OPEN TO OPERATOR, add: "7. **TICK and DEEP fail, TOUCH clears.** Both 'CLOSED FOR GOOD if it fails under DEEP too' and 'CLOSED if it clears only under TOUCH' name this event. Default if silent: `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED`. Naming rival (i) makes it CLOSED FOR GOOD."

findings.finding: The kill's qualifier asserts a cause the line cannot tell apart. L-X.9 prints `ONE-ASSET DEPENDENT (LOAO k/N)` whenever fewer than 3 of 5 leave-one-out panels exclude zero from above. X's own structure note (x_rec/tierc11x/LEANS_X.md:695-696) says "LOAO panels have 4 clusters (35 compositions), and P(an asset appears ≥ 3 of 4 times) = 0.0508 > 0.05. So a single strongly negative asset fails all 4 panels that contain it" — a book DRAGGED by one asset also reads k = 1 of 5, with the only passing panel the one that drops it. That is the opposite of a result carried by one asset.
findings.consequence: A NOT SUPPORTED caused by one losing asset would be reported as dependence on one asset; the wording misstates what was found.
findings.fix: L-X.9 and L-S.28: the qualifier text becomes `LOAO BELOW THE LINE (k/N above; passing when dropped: <assets>; failing when dropped: <assets>)`, and the verdict text adds the fixed sentence "the contract reads one-asset dependence by this line (:106); a panel that fails when an asset is DROPPED leans on that asset, a panel that fails while an asset is KEPT is dragged by it". The word and the rule for D are unchanged.

findings.finding: `stable_across_seeds` (L-X.8: "does the frozen rule give the same word at the sensitivity seed") and SEED-FRAGILE (L-X.14: "the frozen rule at either seed gives another word than the same rule on the exact enumeration (`lo_exact > 0 AND p_exact ≤ bar`)") are undefined for P-SCALP-3. findings.consequence: The builder must guess how to compute two filed flags on the scalper row; they decide nothing, but they are printed in §0.

P-SCALP-3 also files `fill_ladder.<book>.C_sens`, `one_asset.D_sens` and `word_stable_across_seeds` (the six-case table evaluated on the sensitivity-seed tuple equals the word of record)." findings.finding: L-X.14's collared `literal_bar` leaf prints a boolean `clears_literal_bar`, while L-0.16 rules "No collared table holds a verdict word or a column named for a verdict, a cleared bar or a spent test". findings.consequence: A rival verdict flag sits in a Tier-E leaf against L-0.16; the two sections disagree and the fixture cannot see it.

findings.finding: F-DIR (b)'s frozen sample rule is undefined when the refused set holds fewer than three campaigns: "**D3** the first other refused campaign whose deciding acceptance is printed at the entry bar itself … and, if that class is empty (printed NONE-EXISTS with its count asserted zero), the first other refused campaign" presumes a third refusal exists; leg (d) covers only the zero case (`REFUSES-NOTHING`). findings.finding: Sub-stages have ids but no law. findings.consequence: F-RESUME cannot compute a resume point for Stage R; builders start stages on children that are not complete; the scorer looks for a record nobody writes.

findings.finding: instants_of(frame, kind) has no frame contract and its key does not fit every book. L-V.19 fixes the stamp key as '[book, symbol, entry_ms, instant_kind, instant_ms]' and takes events 'through the regbook-schema frame'; L-C.11 hands it TC11-schema campaign frames (arm_close_ms, latch_1r_open_ms, harvest_close_ms, exit_event_ms, exit_event_stamp); L-R.31 declares 'kind {lens, start: "entry"}' with ev_t1_ms; L-S.30 keys VA_STAMPS_scalp on '[book, symbol, trigger_close_ms, instant_kind, instant_ms]' (a MISS has no entry bar), adds expiry / cancel instants and changes bar_close to 'every 1h CLOSE ... not every 5m close' against L-V.19's 'every close of the campaign's own lens'; L-S INTERFACE asks L-V to accept this and L-V does not say so.

findings.fix: L-V.19: 'instants_of(frame, kind). kind is a dict filed in the stamp table's manifest: {book, lens, key: [frame columns after symbol], start_col, end_col, bar_close_lens (default = lens), events: [{name, col, stamp in {close, open_of_bar}, post_event: bool}]}. The frame holds symbol, the key columns and every named column as int64 ms (null = did not happen). Stamp table key = [book, symbol] + key + [instant_kind, instant_ms].' Declared kinds: v6 and trg912 - key [entry_ms], start_col arm_close_ms, end_col exit_event_ms, events arm, entry, plus_1r (latch_1r_open_ms, open_of_bar, post), harvest (harvest_close_ms), bell and exit from exit_event_ms by exit_reason and exit_event_stamp, as_of_pin from open_at_asof; P-SFP books - key [entry_ms], start_col entry_close_ms, events entry, ev_t1 (post), exit (post), as_of_pin; scalper - key [event_ms] (the trigger close, BLD-20), lens 5m, bar_close_lens 1h, events arm, entry (post), ev_t1 (post), exit (post), expiry, cancel. L-L.25's typed row for VA_STAMPS follows this key.

findings.finding: The five spec blocks are carried into the registry as text, but three fields the filer or scorer must MACHINE-READ are written in three dialects, and L-X.18 gives no grammar. (1) Checked fields: L-G writes 'prior: 50 (contract :53 ...)', L-R 'prior: 45 - parsed ...', L-S 'prior: 30% - parsed ...'; same spread for family, family_m, family_bar; L-G and L-R can only 'assume the filer's carry law checks the leading token'. (2) preconditions: L-X.10 says the field 'is none or a list of items {record, certified_by, selector, required}'; P-ADM-1 / P-BRD-1 / P-DIR-1 write 'none.' followed by a paragraph of sha pins; P-SFP-VA-1 writes prose sub-bullets ('selector ..., required "PASS" - the licence row ...'); P-SCALP-3 writes braces. (3) labels: L-X.13 needs {tag, label, text, items} and cuts the clause from 'pre_seen.text up to its first top-level ;' - L-G uses one line with middle-dot separators, L-R sub-bullets, L-S semicolons.
findings.consequence: The write-once filing either HALTs on a dialect or files fields the scorer cannot parse the same way twice; the precondition evaluator and the verdict-cell builder each guess.
findings.fix: L-X.18 adds a FIELD GRAMMAR: (1) id, family, family_m, family_bar, prior: the value is the text up to the first space; anything after it is citation, kept in the plan and dropped from the body key; prior is digits only (L-S writes '30'). (2) preconditions: either the bare word 'none' followed only by text after ' - ' (never evaluated), or sub-bullets each of the form '{record: <path>, certified_by: <progress record> <key>, selector: <selector>, required: <"string" | contains "string" | true | > 0>}' optionally followed by ' - commentary'; HALT PRECOND-GRAMMAR otherwise. HALT-grade input pins move to the 'arms' field under a sub-bullet starting 'inputs pinned:'. (3) labels: one sub-bullet per key: '<key> - tag: <TAG|none>; label: <label>; text: "<text>"; items: <items>', the text being the first double-quoted string. Rewrite the five blocks to it (P-SFP-VA-1's two items in brace form; the P-ADM-1 / P-BRD-1 / P-DIR-1 pin paragraphs into arms).

findings.finding: The pin-map schema cannot hold the pins the sections file. L-0.17: a row has 'regex (one capture group)'; L-0.23: 'Each token names exactly one pin', and F-VETO 'FAILS IF a token of :135-137 has no pin-map row or two'. findings.finding: The hand-sample law for a category or a population that is too small is written five ways. L-0.14: 'an empty category prints NONE-EXISTS and asserts the book's count of it is zero'. L-V F-STATE: 'a class with no member at all makes the leg VOID and RED'. L-G.14: NONE-EXISTS and 'its slot is filled by the next campaign in the same order (labelled FILL)'. L-R.25: NONE-EXISTS, 'carried to the report as a finding', no fill. L-S.31: next unchosen row walked, but 'fewer than three trades in the book is RED' and (unverified list) 'fewer than three trades or three misses makes the leg RED and returns to the orchestrator'. L-R.7 does not say what F-DIR does when fewer than three campaigns are refused.
findings.consequence: A contract fixture goes RED, and blocks TC12-FIX, because a registered BOOK came out small - an outcome-dependent stop that hands the orchestrator an amendment decision after the book is seen; the same event is GREEN in another section.
findings.fix: L-0.14, one law for every section: 'A category with no member prints NONE-EXISTS, asserts from the book that its count is zero, and its slot is taken by the next unchosen row in key order (labelled FILL). If the population holds fewer rows than the contract's count k, the leg hand-verifies ALL of them, prints POPULATION n < k, is GREEN, and the shortfall is a finding-not-fixed owned by the operator. No hand-sample leg is RED or VOID on the size or composition of a book; only a mismatch between the fixture's derivation and production is RED.' Conform L-V F-STATE (a) (drop 'VOID and RED'), L-R.7 (b), L-R.25 (a), L-S.31 (a), (b) and L-S's unverified list.

findings.finding: Five fixtures read 'the hook's open log of a stage build' and no section says where it is. L-0.30 5m leg (a): 'a 5m kline path appears in the env hook's open log of a stage build outside the typed list'; L-S.1 F-SCALP (g): 'the hook's open log of a build holds a path outside the read set'; L-D.27: 'each stage's fixture asserts that every path the hook logged ... was first verified'; L-L.9: 'The stage's hook log must hold no other snapshot path'; L-0.13 F-WARRANTY (a). The referee's log is the in-memory dict _OPENED of ONE process (scripts/tierc11_env.py:1062-1063, opened_paths() :1161-1163): a fixture is another process, and with 'one spawn worker per cell / per asset' (L-V.24, L-S.33) the parent never sees the workers' opens.
findings.consequence: The read-set and 5m-reader legs are either vacuous (they see the fixture's own opens) or each stage invents a private dump format; BLD-01's VA-BLIND proof has nothing to read.
findings.fix: L-D.26 hunk 10 adds 'E.read_set() -> {class: sorted repo- or snapshot-relative paths} of every open since the hook was armed'. L-0.13's manifest helper writes '<dir>/READ_SET.json = the sorted union of E.read_set() over the builder process and its spawn workers (each worker returns its set with its result; merged in key order)', a member of the directory's determinism set. L-0.30 (a), F-SCALP (g), L-D.27's verified-read law, L-L.9 and the VA-BLIND leg read that file and re-derive it in the F-DET twin.

findings.finding: L-0.22 leg (iv): 'subprocess appears only at the typed call sites SUBPROC_SITE_T: the attestation tool's one git helper ... and whatever single site L-D declares for the snapshot clone', and E.hook_escapes flags any 'import subprocess' (scripts/tierc11_env.py:1205, _ESC_MODULES). Two non-fixture modules L-X defines need more: scripts/tierc12_tc11_stamp.py ('a fresh git clone --local ...; TC11's scorer and the suites of TC11's last sweep run THERE', L-X.34) and scripts/tierc12_close.py (BOX_COST 'measures, with git read-only verbs', L-X.31; trace kind 'git', L-X.29). L-X also filed three differences L-0 never ruled: L-0.26's ACTS leg forbids 'any TC12 source' holding a push / merge string, 'import publish_exchange' or a call named publish, which the close generator's template of close_acts.sh must contain; L-0.16 limits the registered marker to 'score documents and section 0' while L-X.28 re-quotes P-SCALP-3 under it in section 4.
findings.consequence: F-HOOK-ESCAPE and F-NOT (ACTS) are RED on the close generator and the stamp tool as specified, or exemptions get added after the freeze with nobody ruling them.
findings.fix: L-0.22 (iv): 'SUBPROC_SITE_T (typed, closed, one pinned call site each, TC11's AM8_SITE_T form): tierc12_data.clone_snapshot (cp -cpR); tierc12_worktree_attest.git (worktree, rev-parse, status, show); tierc12_close.git_ro (read-only verbs rev-parse, log, ls-files, ls-tree, cat-file, show, merge-base, each with --no-optional-locks); tierc12_tc11_stamp.run (git worktree add / remove on the scratch proof tree, and the interpreter running TC11's suites with cwd asserted inside that tree). hook_escapes findings are filtered by exactly these sites.' L-0.26 ACTS: 'the tokens push, merge, publish( and import publish_exchange are permitted only inside the string constant ACTS_TEMPLATE of scripts/tierc12_close.py and in the generated close/close_acts.sh; the leg asserts no call's argv derives from that constant.' L-0.16: 'the registered marker is allowed in score documents, section 0, and section 4's verbatim re-quote of P-SCALP-3's verdict_text'.

findings.finding: L-X.33's F-CLOSE-SCRIPT runs 'steps 1-7 ... in a sandbox clone against a local bare origin, cut before publish()'. Step 2 is the ferry of record: tierc12_ferry.py --of-record is 'shim-armed' and 're-hashes every source and every staged CSV against the tracked manifest (the FRESH leg; a moved sha STOPS the act)' (L-L.32) - the sources are git-ignored parquet and the staged CSVs live under an ignored _det_staged/, so neither exists in a clone. Step 4 runs tierc12_tc11_stamp.py --prove, i.e. a full roll of TC11's suites (L-X.34), inside the fixture. L-0.26 says the acts' 'only executions are bash -n and its step 0 against scratch repositories'; L-X notes the difference 'for the reviser' and nobody ruled it.
findings.consequence: The sandbox leg cannot pass as written (it STOPs at step 2) or costs two more TC11 sweeps per run; L-0.26 and L-X.33 state contradictory execution laws for the acts.
findings.fix: L-X.33: 'the sandbox leg runs a SCRATCH COPY produced by the same generator with two typed substitution points - the step-2 planner call and the step-4 stamp call are replaced by stubs that write their expected outputs (a copy list naming one planted CSV; a planted BUILT line with no re-pin) - and proves ORDER and the STOP guards only. The real planner is proven by F-ROWS leg ACT and the real stamp by F-TC11-STAMP.' L-0.26: 'its only executions are bash -n, step 0 with --check against scratch repositories, and the stubbed sandbox run of a scratch copy with every path outside both trees'.

findings.finding: The tc11-stamp proof environment is under-staged. L-X.34 --prove: 'a fresh git clone --local of the main tree at HEAD into a scratch directory outside both trees; TC11's ignored parquet staged into it by copy (the globs of TC11's attest tool)'; L-0.24 the same. Those globs are STAGE_GLOBS = research_outputs/tierc11/**/*.parquet plus two TC10 files (scripts/tierc11_worktree_attest.py:65-71). TC11's suites read the eight TC10_ALLOW records through tc10_record(), which returns MAIN_TREE / rel (scripts/tierc11_env.py:1170-1176), and _main_tree() returns the tree itself unless .git is a 'gitdir:' file (:216-230). In a clone .git is a directory, so MAIN_TREE is the clone - and all eight allow-listed records are untracked in main [git ls-files: 0 of 8 tracked, e.g. panel/control_journal.parquet, STEP0_RECORD.json], hence absent. TC11's own certified runs were in LINKED worktrees, where MAIN_TREE resolved to the real main tree.
findings.consequence: TC11's sweep goes RED in the clone on missing TC10 records before any stamp is tested; by L-0.24 the acts then 'carry NO stamp step' and the contract's enacted Q2 default lapses for an environment reason, reported as if the cascade had failed.
findings.fix: L-X.34 --prove: 'the proof tree is a DETACHED LINKED WORKTREE of the main repository at HEAD under a scratch directory (git worktree add --detach; removed with --force at the end; no ref and no main-tree file moves), so that TC11's _main_tree() resolves the real main tree and the TC10 allow-list is read there read-only, as in TC11's certified lens runs; TC11's ignored parquet and TC10_STAGED are staged by the attest tool's globs. A PRE leg first runs TC11's sweep on the UNSTAMPED proof tree and must be GREEN; a RED PRE leg is reported PROOF ENVIRONMENT DEFECT and is not a tc11-stamp result.' F-TC11-STAMP gains '(0) PRE: the unstamped sweep is not GREEN'. L-0.24's 'SCRATCH CLONE' wording is conformed. The tool never imports E.

findings.finding: TC12's own close acts break pins TC12 files. (a) L-0.24 moves, at step 4, 'scripts/tierc11_score.py:220 and :224', tierc11_stage_g.py:170, T11/registrations/REGISTRATIONS.json (one leaf) and T11/PROGRESS.json. TC12 pins those files by WHOLE-FILE sha: L-X.24 reads the sixteen columns 'by ast from scripts/tierc11_score.py:248-255, sha asserted'; L-G.5 reads the lag cut from 'REGISTRATIONS.json (sha on record 648834bf...f1ee, read through E.tc11_record)' and the P-ADM-1 block freezes that sha in its text; L-D.27's tc11_record certifies every TC11 read against T11/PROGRESS.json, 'itself asserted against progress/TC12-R0.json'. Only L-L saw it: 'The spec pins the PAYLOAD shas and TC11's chain head, never TC11's whole-file registrations sha (the tc11-stamp close act moves the file sha)'. (b) L-0.1 says the contract's whole-file sha is 'compared by nothing afterwards', but scripts/tierc12_progress.py:54 writes it into PROGRESS.json contract_of_record, and F-PROGRESS requires PROGRESS.json byte-equal to a re-derivation - which TC12's own BUILT stamp changes.
findings.consequence: After the operator's keystrokes TC12's scorer, Stage G builder, tc11_record and F-PROGRESS can no longer re-pass - the FN-M-QUEUE-STAMP defect the 'tc11-stamp' ruling exists to cure, re-created one tier down, with a registration text citing a sha the tier itself invalidates.

findings.finding: L-D.23 defines TickGrid on floats: 'dec(x) = Decimal(repr(float(x)))', and floor_ticks / ceil_ticks take x. L-S forms two quantities EXACTLY in decimal before snapping - T2 'formed EXACTLY in decimal from dec(FAR), dec(ATR) and the pin's fraction, then snapped' (L-S.11) and DEEP's depth 'ceil_ticks(deep_atr * ATR_1h[k1]), the product formed exactly in decimal' (L-S.15) - and its INTERFACE says L-D.23 'does not state' that the functions accept a Decimal: 'If L-D declines, the float ... is passed and F-SCALP (d) counts every order where the exact rational result lands on another tick (required zero, else HALT for an amendment).'
findings.consequence: The scalper's target and DEEP levels are computed one of two ways depending on what the TickGrid builder happens to accept, with a HALT-and-amend path that opens only after orders exist.
findings.fix: L-D.23: 'floor_ticks, ceil_ticks, on_grid and the four comparisons accept float or decimal.Decimal. A Decimal is used exactly as given (finite, > 0; no float round-trip); a float goes through dec. All arithmetic stays inside the trapping context.' F-TICK (a) enumerates Decimal inputs carrying more significant digits than a float64 round-trips. Delete L-S INTERFACE's 'If L-D declines ...' fallback and the matching line of L-S's unverified list.

findings.finding: L-R.29 builds a second implementation of the V2 machine inside a decision module: 'The machine on a box - a mirror of static_box_machine with V2's three constants ... a close beyond an edge opens a breach; back at or inside within K is a swing failure ...; N closes beyond or one close M*ATR beyond ... is the acceptance', held equal to value_area.va_machine by F-NULL-MIRROR (b) ('a fixture may import the module; no builder does'). findings.consequence: Two V2 machines exist, one outside the wall, with equality resting on a fixture import the ruling's letter does not allow; the reviser must guess whether L-R.29 or L-R.17's argument governs.
findings.fix: Decide for the single implementation, consistent with L-V.23: 'the gaps+order schedule and its box machine run in the DOOR. scripts/tierc12_va.py mirrors tierc10_null.schedule (L-R.29's law, seed stream and lead-gap floor unchanged), runs value_area.va_machine on arrays held constant at each box's edges, and files va/va_null_go_boxes.parquet (key [lens, asset, draw, box]: src_rid, confirm_i, life, censored, bot, top, u, lead_gap_swapped) and va/va_null_go_events.parquet (the L-V.14 schema plus draw, box). tierc12_stage_r_tables.py reads the two files and computes its statistics; it implements no acceptance, swing-failure or lapse test.' findings.finding: Small process gaps in L-0. (1) L-0.11 writes wall time and load to 'T12/sweep/clock/<STAGE>.json, which is not an artifact', and L-0.4 quarantines into 'T12/_partial_<ts>/'; neither path is ignored by the nested .gitignore (it ignores only **/*.parquet, **/_det_*/ and x_rec/**) [git check-ignore: no match], so both sit untracked-but-not-ignored in the main tree. (2) The sweep runs 'once inside the reproducibility lens with --root=<scratch>', but the roll is 'the suite strings of that stage's fixture records' verbatim; no reading says every suite accepts --root or how it is appended. (3) The suites table files the closure suite at 'TC12-REG (AST legs)', but leg (iv) calls E.hook_escapes and E cannot be imported before TC12-D (L-D.26 P3). (4) TC12-REG and TC12-ENV each have two or three producing sections and one progress record with no named writer (O-6: 'Each stage builder writes progress/<STAGE>.json').
findings.consequence: Clock files (which hold timings) can be swept into a commit by a careless pathspec and are seen by every disk-walk fixture; the reviewer's sweep invocation is undefined; a REG-stage leg cannot run; two builders race for one record.
findings.fix: (1) 'clock files go to T12/sweep/_det_clock/<STAGE>.json; quarantine directories are named T12/_det_partial_<ts>/' (both then fall under the existing **/_det_*/ rule; no ignore file is edited). (2) L-0.11: 'every tierc12_*_fixtures.py accepts --root=DIR (all writes, transcripts and twins under DIR); the sweep appends it to each recorded invocation'. (3) Suites table: 'at --stage=TC12-REG the closure suite runs F-TYPED, F-SEED, F-FX-MIRROR, F-FX-FORM and F-CLOSURE (ii)-(iii); legs (i), (i-b), (iv), (v) first run at TC12-ENV'. (4) L-0.9: 'the parent record of a stage with several producers is written by the orchestrator's gate step from the artifact maps each producer returns'.

findings.finding: The two simulators carry opposite gap laws, and P-SFP-VA-1 takes the trader-favouring one on both sides. L-R.19 step 0: "`d·(o[j] − stop) ≤ 0` → the whole open position exits at the STOP price (the v6 law: a stop fills at the stop, through a gap too). Otherwise a resting T1 with `d·(o[j] − T1) ≥ 0` fills at `o[j]`", steps 2-3 fill at `max(T1, o[j])` / `max(T2, o[j])`, and its RIVALS say "Fill at the level on a gap open (X's symmetric-gap twin) — not carried". L-S.18 takes the other law ("when the bar OPENS at or beyond the stop it is filled at the open (the worse price)"; targets at their level) and quotes X on this exact record law: it "favours the trader on both sides" (x_rec/tierc11x/LEANS_X.md:1308-1310: "targets collect the gap; the stop ignores it"). The source confirms the asymmetry: x_rec/scripts/tc11x_sfp.py:567-601, where `gap_sym=False` books `float(stop)` on a gap and `_fill` returns `max(level, o)`. Gap bars are not hypothetical on this tape: LEANS_X.md:1314-1316 files 859 1h bars on NEAR and 70 on ZEC with |open − prior close| > 0.1 ATR. L-S's INTERFACE asks L-R to "either agree or state the difference" on this choice; L-R states none. L-R.12 also says the half "rests there as a limit" while L-R.20 books "taker on every leg", so the order type that decides the gap price is unstated.
findings.consequence: A registered vs-zero row would be scored with stops that never pay a gap and targets that always collect one. Two rows of one tier would answer the same contract silence in opposite directions, with the optimistic answer on the row that has the tighter bar (0.05).
findings.fix: Replace L-R.19 steps 0-3 with X's symmetric law (`bar_step(..., gap_sym=True)`): "0. THE OPEN decides first. `d·(o[j] − stop) ≤ 0` → the whole open position exits at the OPEN `o[j]` (a stop-market fills at the first print; `gap_stop` iff `d·(o[j] − stop) < 0`). Otherwise a T1 with `d·(o[j] − T1) ≥ 0` fills at the LEVEL T1 and a T2 with `d·(o[j] − T2) ≥ 0` exits the remainder at the LEVEL T2 (`gap_t1`, `gap_t2` counted; no gap improvement). 1. STOP adverse-first at the stop price. 2. T1 at T1. 3. T2 at T2, same bar if reached." Add to L-R.12: "T1 and T2 are touch-triggered TAKER exits booked at their level." Every twin and the 1d cell inherit the law. F-SFP-MIRROR runs the mirrored step with `gap_sym=False` against X's filed record rows (a second declared switch beside the invalidation switch) and with `gap_sym=True` against the `symmetric_gap` rows of x_rec/tierc11x/sfp/X2_twins.parquet (that book exists for 1h and 4h). L-R.19's plant "a stop filled at the open on a gap" becomes "a gap stop booked at the stop price". The REGISTRATION SPEC walk sentence becomes: "the open decides first — a bar opening at or beyond the stop exits at the open, a bar opening at or beyond a target fills it at the target level; then the stop, adverse-first, at the stop price; then T1 at T1; then T2 at T2". L-R states the one remaining difference from L-S.18 (the 5m walk has no open-first step for targets).

findings.finding: L-X.24: "**Cross-arm law on P-SCALP-3:** `n(ladder__touch) ≥ n(scored) ≥ n(ladder__deep)`, else HALT `LADDER-ORDER`." The three fill books are separately sequenced (L-S.16: "Each walk has ITS OWN one-order / one-position sequence … Book totals are printed and are NOT a theorem … a touch-only fill can block triggers the record would have traded"), and scout U6 H14 records that X's own ridden twins are not ordered by n. O-32 fixes the ordering "per order". The filed P-SCALP-3 spec also omits what L-S.28 promises: its verdict_rule lists "the fill-sensitivity row (per fill rule n, point, interval, p, C(X)), the LOAO line k/N and the single-trade share" and no per-order ladder counts or non-monotone disclosure.
findings.consequence: The scorer can HALT P-SCALP-3 with no defect in any book; a HALTed row prints no word and blocks CLOSE (L-X.7). The other way out is a builder forcing a shared order sequence to satisfy the HALT, which is a different book from the one L-S specifies. Either way the reader is not told in the filed text that the three n are not comparable order for order.
findings.fix: Replace the L-X.24 sentence with: "**Ladder law on P-SCALP-3 (O-32, per order):** each of the three arms' sidecars carries `n_orders`, `n_filled_touch`, `n_filled_tick`, `n_filled_deep` — the three entry tests of L-S.15 evaluated on that arm's own orders (L-S.16) — and the scorer HALTs `LADDER-ORDER` unless `n_filled_touch ≥ n_filled_tick ≥ n_filled_deep` on every arm. The arm totals `n(ladder__touch)`, `n(scored)`, `n(ladder__deep)` are printed beside and are not ordered by law (three separately sequenced books); when they are not ordered the row carries the note `BOOK-N-NOT-MONOTONE`, a disclosure, never a HALT and never a qualifier." Add to the verdict_rule of L-S's REGISTRATION SPEC, after "the single-trade share of record": "then the per-order ladder counts of the TICK ledger and, where the three books' own n are not ordered, the line BOOK-N-NOT-MONOTONE (the books are sequenced separately; their n are not comparable order for order)".

findings.finding: The same contract sentence ("TARGET 1 = POC (half off); TARGET 2 = far edge − 0.25 ATR (remainder)", with "rr-min" as the only written skip, :73-74 and :100) gets two degenerate-geometry laws. L-R.14 refuses an event when "`d·(T1 − e) ≤ thr` — the POC is at, behind, or within the fee band of the entry (`t1_within_10bps`)", when "`d·(T2 − e) ≤ thr`", and when "`d·(T2 − T1) ≤ 0` … (`targets_inverted`)". L-S.11 does the opposite on both: "X's refusal of a target within 10 bps of entry (LX-X2.6) is NOT carried: this contract's only skip is \"rr-min\" (L-S.12), and removing near-zero T1 trades could only raise a mean", and a POC at or beyond T2 is "A void T1 … T2 takes the whole position … not a filter". L-S's stated reason applies with equal force to P-SFP-VA-1: the refusal removes trades whose T1 half cannot net above zero after two fees. `targets_inverted` also refuses a geometry that has already passed rr-min. L-S's INTERFACE asks for agreement or a stated difference on the void-T1 choice; L-R states none.
findings.consequence: P-SFP-VA-1 would carry two filters the contract does not write (a typed-origin 10 bps band and a targets-inverted refusal), on the side L-S itself says can only help a mean. One tier would answer "POC equal or near the entry" and "POC beyond T2" two ways.

findings.finding: Two registered range trades read the same contract words with opposite defaults, and the more favourable one carries no twin and no operator item. The contract names one skip for both ('Minimum reward at T2 ≥ 1.5 × stop ... or the trade is skipped; the unfiltered twin printed', :73-74, :100). L-R.14 adds three: an event 'is REFUSED and counted, before the reward test' when 'the POC is at, behind, or within the fee band of the entry (`t1_within_10bps`)', when T2 is within the band, or when 'T2 is not beyond T1 (`targets_inverted`)'; its rival 'T1-collapse ... not carried as a book'. L-S.11 on the same clause: 'X's refusal of a target within 10 bps of entry (LX-X2.6) is NOT carried: this contract's only skip is rr-min, and removing near-zero T1 trades could only raise a mean', and a POC at or beyond T2 makes T1 void. Likewise L-R.19: a stop fills 'at the STOP price ... through a gap too' and the open decides targets first, 'X's symmetric-gap twin — not carried'; L-S.18: the stop fills 'at the open (the worse price)', stop first unconditionally, noting X's own remark that the record 'favours the trader on both sides'. L-S's interface lists the three differences; no OPEN TO OPERATOR list does.
findings.consequence: P-SFP-VA-1's registered book excludes trades by a rule the contract does not state, with a mechanism — stated by the sibling section — by which the exclusion can only help its mean, and nothing printed shows the excluded trades' book.
findings.fix: One law for both rows, written in L-R: L-R.14 refuses only `stop_none` and `d·(T1 − e) ≤ 0` (the contract's 'toward the POC' cannot hold); an event with the POC inside the fee band trades as written (`t1_within_fee_band`, counted); `d·(T2 − T1) ≤ 0` makes T1 void and the whole position rests at T2 (L-S.11's law); T2 within the band is left to rr-min. L-R.19 fills a stop at the worse of stop and open and tests the stop before any target (L-S.18). F-SFP-MIRROR keeps X's refusal and gap laws switched on for the mirror leg only. If the orchestrator keeps X's laws on the record instead, L-R ships `tierE__geometry_kept` and `tierE__gap_sym` and both differences enter OPEN TO OPERATOR.

findings.finding: F-ROLL's name-to-block map is described and not given, and the block ids in use do not share a grammar. L-0.19: 'A contract name maps to its blocks by a typed pattern table (TC11's form: the name `import-closure` matches blocks whose id starts `F-CLOSURE`)' — no table. In use: `F-LEDGER` beside L-X's `F-LEDGER-FMT` (L-L: 'a prefix pattern would also match'); `F-SFP` beside `F-SFP-ASOF` and `F-SFP-MIRROR`; `F-STATE` beside `F-STATE-X`; `F-GATE [P-ADM-1]` and `F-GATE [P-BRD-1]` (a space and brackets; TC11's id pattern at `scripts/tierc11_close.py:2045` is `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`); `F-GRID (era)`; 'F-TOLL, data half ... also named F-D-FEE'.
